title: The Tide That Did Not Return

nodes.title: The Keeper's Final Note
nodes.brief: You stand in the salt-crusted lamp room of Gullmouth lighthouse, reading the sealed note Orsolya Venn left before vanishing into the bare seabed.
nodes.page: On the Gullmouth lighthouse lamp room glass, salt crusts and frosts the windows against a horizon that should be blue water but is only brown, baked mud. Three days ago, the sea simply emptied out. Now, the Low stretches bare to the edge of the world, littered with the rotting ribs of stranded ships and bloated whale carcasses. In the suffocating quiet of the high tower you hold a folded piece of parchment sealed with Orsolya Venn's wax stamp. Your mentor is gone. Her note is brief, jagged with haste. It speaks of the Meridian Gear, the ancient mechanism the old Tidewardens built beneath the Sunken Stair. She writes that it has jammed, and whoever forces the great brass wheel to turn will decide which coast the ocean claims first. Orsolya has gone down into the dry deep to find it. As a licensed wrecker, your duty is to salvage what is left behind, but this is a prize that could reshape the world.

nodes.title: The Keeper's Quarters
nodes.brief: Gullmouth Lighthouse: You search the abandoned keeper's quarters for any useful gear or lingering clues before descending the cliff to the dried-out harbour below.
nodes.page:
Dust motes drift in the cold beams of sunlight piercing the keeper's quarters. Orsolya left in a hurry; her heavy woollen shawl still hangs over the chair, smelling faint of pipe smoke and dried kelp. Beyond the salt-rimed window, the dry expanse of the Low stretches out, a vast brown scab where the sea used to be. You need to gather what you can before descending the cliff path to the dead harbour.

The room is a clutter of the old keeper's eccentricities. Faded navigational charts scatter across the oak desk, tracing routes through sinkholes and reefs now open to the air. On the stone balcony, a rusted brass spyglass lies abandoned beside a coiled rope. Half-dismantled by the hearth, a lantern sloshes with precious whale oil. The path down to the boats waits outside, steep and unforgiving.

exits.label: Dismantle the heavy lantern for oil
Climb down the treacherous cliff path

nodes.title: Faded Navigational Charts
nodes.brief: You decipher a set of faded navigational charts left scattered across the desk, risking a headache to uncover a hidden safe route through the sinkholes.
nodes.page:
Parchment crackles under your fingers as you smooth out the oversized maps on Orsolya's drafting table. Most of the documents depict the Wrack Coast as it was four days ago, covered in deep, treacherous currents. However, one heavy vellum sheet has been frantically scrawled over with fresh charcoal. Orsolya has attempted to map the newly exposed Low. The drawing marks the terrifying sinkholes that have opened up in the salt-flats, craters that swallow scavengers whole. A winding, convoluted path weaves through the hazard, but the notation is incredibly dense, layered with tide-clock calculations and obscure wrecker shorthand. Deciphering this route will require intense focus. Staring at the tiny, frantic numbers is already making your vision swim and a dull ache throb behind your eyes.

You need to understand this path if you want to navigate the dry seabed without falling into the dark.

exits.label: Try to read the safe route

nodes.title: Deciphering the Route
nodes.brief: You decipher a set of faded navigational charts left scattered across the desk, risking a headache to uncover a hidden safe route through the sinkholes.
nodes.page: Squinting against the glare of the morning sun, you lean heavily over the desk and try to force the charcoal symbols to make sense. The calculations are erratic, mixing standard fathom-depths with bizarre astrological symbols the Drift Pilgrims use to track the moon. To make matters worse, Orsolya's handwriting degrades near the edges of the page, turning into a frantic scribble. You rub your temples, trying to push through the mounting pressure in your skull. If you cannot parse the logic behind these markings, you will be walking blind into a terrain that has not seen the sky in a thousand years. You trace a soot-stained finger along the jagged line, holding your breath as you try to anticipate the old lighthouse keeper's frantic train of thought.

nodes.title: A Blinding Headache
nodes.brief: You decipher a set of faded navigational charts left scattered across the desk, risking a headache to uncover a hidden safe route through the sinkholes.
nodes.page: Pain spikes sharply behind your eyes, a sudden and searing migraine that forces you to stagger back from the desk. You knock an inkwell to the floor, shattering the glass and ruining a pile of blank ledgers. The charcoal numbers on the map blur into a meaningless grey smudge. You spend nearly an hour sitting on the floor with your head between your knees, waiting for the nausea and the throbbing ache to pass. By the time you can see straight again, the sun has climbed much higher in the sky, wasting precious daylight. You have lost the thread of Orsolya's logic, leaving the safe path through the sinkholes a mystery. With a frustrated sigh, you push yourself upright, knowing you will have to trust your own instincts on the salt-flats.

nodes.title: The Safe Path
nodes.brief: You decipher a set of faded navigational charts left scattered across the desk, risking a headache to uncover a hidden safe route through the sinkholes.
nodes.page: Suddenly the chaotic scribbles align into a clear picture. Your eyes clear. The final charcoal line traces to a rocky outcropping near the Singing Dunes. Orsolya was using the shadow of the stranded leviathan carcass to triangulate the stable ground beneath that mark. You fold the vellum map and tuck it inside your coat, a prize that might keep you from plummeting into a lightless subterranean sea. The knowledge is yours. You step away from the drafting table. The Low is a deathtrap, but you now hold the key to navigating its most treacherous expanse.

nodes.title: The Rusted Spyglass
nodes.brief: You try to repair a rusted spyglass found on the balcony, risking cutting your hands to gain a valuable tool for spotting distant scavengers.
nodes.page:
Outside on the balcony, the wind tastes entirely of dry salt and dead kelp. Resting on a salt-rimed crate is a collapsible brass spyglass, a heavy, expensive piece of equipment that Orsolya must have dropped in her haste. When you pick it up, the metal is cold and stubbornly rigid. The sea-spray has corroded the sliding joints, fusing the brass cylinders together. Spotting rival wrecker crews or aggressive Drift Pilgrims from a distance would be an immense advantage out on the open seabed. However, the brass edges are sharp and jagged where the casing has split. Forcing the mechanism open is going to take leverage and raw strength, and one slip could slice your palms open on the rusted metal.

Both hands find the casing, and you prepare to twist.

nodes.title: A Delicate Operation
nodes.brief: You try to repair a rusted spyglass found on the balcony, risking cutting your hands to gain a valuable tool for spotting distant scavengers.
nodes.page:
Bracing the spyglass against the wooden railing, you examine the corroded mechanism more closely. The salt crust is thickest near the primary lens housing, sealing the fragile glass behind a wall of green verdigris. To truly make this tool useful, you will need to dismantle the housing completely and clean the internal tracks. The work is delicate and frustrating, and the rusted edges of the brass casing are sharp enough to slice a wrecker's thick calluses if a finger slips. A deep cut would invite infection from the stagnant rock pools down below.

The harbour waits quietly in the distance, a reminder that time is slipping away while you stand here tinkering with broken glass.

nodes.title: Forcing the Mechanism
nodes.brief: You try to repair a rusted spyglass found on the balcony, risking cutting your hands to gain a valuable tool for spotting distant scavengers.
nodes.page: You wrap a scrap of sailcloth around your palm for protection and wedge your fingers into the cracked brass housing. The metal whines in protest, a terrible screeching sound that echoes off the empty lighthouse walls. You try to apply pressure evenly, working the corroded cylinders back and forth to break the seal of dried salt without shattering the delicate lenses inside. The verdigris flakes away like green snow, but the inner track remains stubbornly jammed. You grit your teeth and push harder, feeling the sharp, jagged edge of the split casing bite through the sailcloth and press dangerously against your skin. You need to snap the rust bond before the metal slices into your hand.

nodes.title: A Costly Slip
nodes.brief: You try to repair a rusted spyglass found on the balcony, risking cutting your hands to gain a valuable tool for spotting distant scavengers.
nodes.page: Blood wells up instantly as the brittle brass casing collapses under your grip. The jagged metal tears right through your makeshift sailcloth protection, slicing a deep, agonizing gash across the meaty part of your palm. You hiss through your teeth, dropping the ruined spyglass onto the balcony where the main lens cracks against the wooden boards. The tool is completely useless now. You spend a frustrating, painful ten minutes wrapping your bleeding hand in clean bandages, pulling the linen tight to stop the red flow. Every movement sends a stinging jolt up your arm. It is a foolish, sloppy mistake, and you will have to navigate the dangerous depths of the Low with a compromised grip.

nodes.title: Clear Vision
nodes.brief: You try to repair a rusted spyglass found on the balcony, risking cutting your hands to gain a valuable tool for spotting distant scavengers.
nodes.page: Grinding loudly, the salt-fused cylinders finally give way with a harsh crack. You manage to ease off the pressure just before the sharp casing bites into your palm, keeping your hands completely intact. Sliding the mechanism back and forth, you clear out the worst of the green verdigris until the spyglass extends smoothly. You lift it to your eye, peering down at the distant, dried-out seabed. Through the slightly cloudy glass, the stranded ships and distant scavengers leap into sharp focus. This is a tremendous advantage. You collapse the spyglass with a satisfying click and slide it securely into your belt, ready to spot danger long before it can reach you out on the bare sand.

nodes.title: The Brass Lantern
nodes.brief: You dismantle a heavy brass lantern to extract its precious oil, risking a spill to secure a vital light source for the dark days ahead.
nodes.page: Dust motes dance in the slanted light of the keeper's quarters as you spot the old storm lantern hanging by the charting desk. It is a heavy, tarnished brass thing, built to withstand a gale. With the sea gone and darkness threatening to choke the streets of Gullmouth once the sun sets, good oil is already a scarce commodity. You unhook it carefully, feeling the slosh of thick fuel in its reservoir. The base is tightly sealed, meant to be opened only with a specialised wrench that is nowhere to be found. You will have to crack it manually.

nodes.title: A Stubborn Seal
nodes.brief: You dismantle a heavy brass lantern to extract its precious oil, risking a spill to secure a vital light source for the dark days ahead.
nodes.page: You set the lantern on the scarred oak table and dig through your pack for a rusted iron pry bar. Brass bites cold under your palms. You seat the flattened edge against the locked reservoir cap and lean on it with slow care. The catch pops once in the quiet room. You wipe a bead of sweat from your brow, because one wrong angle could crack the glass housing or pour the fuel across the floorboards. The cap shifts. A dark, viscous slit opens, sharp with the smell of rendered blubber.

nodes.title: Breaking the Cap
nodes.brief: You dismantle a heavy brass lantern to extract its precious oil, risking a spill to secure a vital light source for the dark days ahead.
nodes.page: Leaning close to the stubborn reservoir, you press your thumb against the brass lip. The metal groans, warped by years of salt and heat. You need to dislodge the rusted cap without tilting the base, an exacting task requiring absolute focus. If you apply too much force, the fragile casing will buckle, sending a ruinous wave of oil soaking into the thirsty wooden planks of the floor. You hold your breath, slotting the pry bar deeper into the groove, feeling the mechanical tension shudder up your forearm. It is a matter of leverage and patience now.

nodes.title: A Messy Spill
nodes.brief: You dismantle a heavy brass lantern to extract its precious oil, risking a spill to secure a vital light source for the dark days ahead.
nodes.page:
Metal shrieks as the cap gives way entirely and throws you off balance. The lantern tips. Before you can right it, a thick arc of amber oil sloshes over the rim, pools over your knuckles, and splashes onto the floorboards, where it soaks into the dry wood with a sickening hiss. You scramble to right the brass base, but the damage is done. Most of the precious fuel is gone. Only a meagre puddle remains in the reservoir, and your hands reek of whale fat.

The smell will stay for days.

nodes.title: Captured Light
nodes.brief: You dismantle a heavy brass lantern to extract its precious oil, risking a spill to secure a vital light source for the dark days ahead.
nodes.page: Wiping your slick hands on a rag, you manage to secure the spoils. You tip the brass reservoir and pour the thick, amber liquid into a sturdy iron flask. The smell is pungent, carrying the deep-sea tang of rendered leviathan fat, but it will burn bright and long in the encroaching dark. You cork the flask tightly and slip it into your pack, feeling a small measure of comfort against the gathering shadows. With this fuel secured, the descent to the harbour will be just a little less daunting.

nodes.title: The Silent Descent
nodes.brief: You climb down the treacherous cliff path to the harbour, greeted by the unsettling silence of stranded fishing boats and the whispering winds.
nodes.page: Leaving the lighthouse behind, you navigate the treacherous switchbacks carved into the sheer chalk of the cliff. The descent to Gullmouth is normally accompanied by the roar of the surf and the chaotic cries of gulls diving for scraps. Today, an unsettling silence presses against your eardrums. Below you, the great harbour sits completely dry. Fishing boats, galleons, and skiffs tilt at grotesque angles, stranded in the drying mud like discarded toys. The wind whistles softly through the rigging of a hundred immobile masts, carrying the scent of rotting kelp and exposed brine. The town clings to the lower cliff face, its people moving like stunned insects through the lower docks. They stare out at the bare horizon where the ocean used to be, a terrible expanse of mud, wrecks, and sudden, plunging ravines. You step off the bottom stair onto the cobblestones of the wharf.

nodes.title: The Dry Harbour
nodes.brief: The Dry Harbour: You navigate the grounded fleet and desperate rival crews, looking for supplies and information before stepping out onto the vast, exposed seabed.
nodes.page: Shadows stretch long across the cracked mud of the dry docks. You walk among the grounded fleet, your boots crunching on salt-crusted detritus. Desperate rival crews of the Wreckers' Guild are already prowling the tilted hulls, tearing copper plating and rigging from ships that will clearly never sail again. You need supplies and information before stepping out onto the vast, exposed seabed of the Low. Ahead, a heavy smuggler's barrel is wedged precariously under the rotting timbers of a listing brigantine. To your left, a knot of hardened wreckers whisper urgently over a torn parchment. Near the harbour wall, a solitary drift pilgrim cowers in the shadow of a dry anchor, clutching a bone relic. The open salt-flats beckon beyond the town limits, vast and terrifying.

nodes.title: The Bitter Net-Mender
nodes.brief: You negotiate with a desperate net-mender for sturdy ropes, risking a harsh argument to secure climbing gear that will help you descend the Sunken Stair.
nodes.page: Tucked in an alley behind the Customs-Priest's shuttered tollhouse, you find a hunched net-mender frantically sorting through a tangle of hemp and wire. The old woman's hands are a blur of calluses and twine. With no water, there are no fish, and her livelihood has vanished overnight. Still, she possesses the finest climbing ropes in Gullmouth, braided strong enough to haul a leviathan carcass. You approach carefully, eyeing a thick coil of black-tarred rope resting by her stool. The Sunken Stair is deep and treacherous; you will not survive the descent without it.

nodes.title: A Desperate Price
nodes.brief: You negotiate with a desperate net-mender for sturdy ropes, risking a harsh argument to secure climbing gear that will help you descend the Sunken Stair.
nodes.page: Looking up from her frantic work, the net-mender fixes you with a hollow, red-rimmed stare. She demands a king's ransom in silver for the rope, an absurd price you cannot possibly meet. When you offer trade, she spits on the cobblestones, insisting that only coin will buy her a ticket on the ferryman's cart - even though the ferryman has nowhere to sail. Her panic makes her stubborn and volatile. You will have to talk her down, finding a way to pierce her hysteria and make her see reason, or you will walk away empty-handed.

nodes.title: Pushing the Bargain
nodes.brief: You negotiate with a desperate net-mender for sturdy ropes, risking a harsh argument to secure climbing gear that will help you descend the Sunken Stair.
nodes.page: Choosing your words with utmost care, you lean against the alley wall. You must convince the old woman that silver is worthless in a town where the sea has died. Food, water, and alliances are the only true currency now. If you push too hard, she will start screaming for the Guild enforcers, drawing the wrong kind of attention to your preparations. You lock eyes with her, modulating your tone to project calm authority while subtly highlighting the bleak reality of her situation. You make your counteroffer, hoping to strike a bargain that leaves her satisfied and secures the vital climbing gear you need.

nodes.title: A Costly Exchange
nodes.brief: You negotiate with a desperate net-mender for sturdy ropes, risking a harsh argument to secure climbing gear that will help you descend the Sunken Stair.
nodes.page: Scowling fiercely, the net-mender rejects your logic with a harsh, barking laugh that echoes down the alley. She accuses you of trying to cheat a starving widow, her voice rising in a shrill crescendo. Several passing wreckers stop to watch the commotion, their hands resting on rusty boat hooks. Forced to back down to avoid a brawl, you hastily press a few of your own meagre rations into her hand just to quiet her down. It is a terrible trade, costing you vital supplies, but she snatches the dried meat greedily and finally kicks the coil of tarred rope toward your boots.

nodes.title: A Fair Accord
nodes.brief: You negotiate with a desperate net-mender for sturdy ropes, risking a harsh argument to secure climbing gear that will help you descend the Sunken Stair.
nodes.page: You gather the prize into your arms and make it fast. The net-mender turns your terms over once more, then nods and takes them. You sling the black-tarred rope over your shoulder. It reeks of pitch and dead salt, but the coil sits firm against your back, and you trust it for the deepest shafts of the Sunken Stair. You leave the alleyway. Behind you the old woman already mutters as she returns to her useless nets.

nodes.title: The Trapped Barrel
nodes.brief: You pry open a sealed smuggler's barrel wedged beneath a rotting hull, risking a collapse to acquire a stash of rare cured meats.
nodes.page:
Lower-dock mud pulls at your calves as you spot the shape of a smuggler's barrel wedged tight beneath the rotting, algae-slick ribs of a grounded trawler. The vessel leans hard. Its timbers groan in the coastal wind, and if that hull shifts it will crush anything beneath it into the seabed before you can drag clear. Still, the salt-crusted wax seal on the barrel promises goods kept sound against the damp.

A tempting prize for a wrecker bound for the Low. You creep closer, testing the mud under your boots, and eye the angle of the trapped cask.

nodes.title: The Smuggler's Stash
nodes.brief: You pry open a sealed smuggler's barrel wedged beneath a rotting hull, risking a collapse to acquire a stash of rare cured meats.
nodes.page:
Wedged deep beneath the splintered ribs of a stranded cog, a smuggler's barrel sits half-buried in the silt. The ship's hull groans in the wind, a rotting cage threatening to collapse at the slightest disturbance. You slide your crowbar under the rusted iron hoop of the barrel, testing the weight above. A shower of barnacles and dry rot rains down on your shoulders as you apply pressure.

With a wet crack, the timber lid gives way. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, lies a small fortune in the current days of famine: a stash of rare, salt-cured meats from the southern archipelagos, untouched by the sea's sudden retreat. Bundles come up fast into your arms while you watch the buckling beams groan in the breeze, and you get clear before the ship becomes your tomb.

exits.label: Slip away from the groaning wreckage

nodes.title: Shifting Timbers
nodes.brief: You pry open a sealed smuggler's barrel wedged beneath a rotting hull, risking a collapse to acquire a stash of rare cured meats.
nodes.page:
Force on the prybar drives the iron rim into the wood. The barrel's lid begins to budge, but the sudden shift sends a harsh vibration straight up into the trawler's damaged hull. Timbers above groan.

Dust and splinters rain down as the ship's mass starts to settle. You ease the lid off the barrel and brace the adjacent planks so the structure does not crash onto you. Force and intuition share the work.

nodes.title: Buried Beneath Rot
nodes.brief: You pry open a sealed smuggler's barrel wedged beneath a rotting hull, risking a collapse to acquire a stash of rare cured meats.
nodes.page:
Wood shrieks as the trawler shifts violently. The massive hull drops a few inches, pins your prybar, and clips your shoulder with brutal force. You throw yourself backward into the mud just as the ribs cave in, burying the smuggler's barrel beneath a pile of splintered debris.

Gasping for breath, you clutch your bruised shoulder. The prize is completely crushed, the rare meats ruined in the muck and shattered timber. Your arm throbs with a deep, aching pain that will slow your progress on the flats. Shaking the mud from your coat, you leave the collapsed wreck behind, nursing your fresh injury and carrying nothing but frustration.

nodes.title: A Hearty Provision
nodes.brief: You pry open a sealed smuggler's barrel wedged beneath a rotting hull, risking a collapse to acquire a stash of rare cured meats.
nodes.page:
With a final, muted pop, the heavy lid comes free just as the hull groans and settles. You snatch the contents and scramble backward into the pale sunlight before the trawler's ribs buckle inward, sending a shower of rotted wood into the mud where you just knelt.

Safe from the collapse, you inspect your prize. Wrapped tightly in oiled canvas are several thick slabs of cured, spiced meat, perfectly preserved and highly valuable in these lean times. It is a hearty provision that will keep your strength up on the long walk ahead, a rare comfort pulled from the wreckage of the dry harbour.

nodes.title: Shadows and Secrets
nodes.brief: You observe a group of rival Wreckers' Guild members to learn their intended path, risking detection to gain a valuable map of the Low.
nodes.page:
Crouched behind a stack of barnacle-encrusted crates, you watch a trio of rival wreckers from the Hook-and-Line crew. They are huddled around a lantern, arguing over a scrap of parchment. You recognise their leader, a scarred net-mender named Harlan, tracing a jagged line across the paper with a grimy finger.

"The Sunken Stair is this way," Harlan mutters, his voice carrying on the salty breeze. "Past the singing dunes and the old coral beds." That parchment is a hand-drawn chart of the newly exposed seabed, tracking hazards and stable paths. If you can get a closer look, or perhaps snatch it while they are distracted, your journey would be vastly safer.

exits.label: Sneak closer for a better look

nodes.title: A Stolen Glance
nodes.brief: You observe a group of rival Wreckers' Guild members to learn their intended path, risking detection to gain a valuable map of the Low.
nodes.page:
Edging along the shadows of the crates, you try to memorise the crude topography Harlan has sketched. The light from their lantern flickers, casting long, distorted shadows across the dry docks. You need more than just a fleeting glance to understand the safe routes through the sinkholes.

One of the crew members turns his head, a sudden motion as a gull cries out overhead. You freeze, pressing your back flat against the damp wood. You must carefully track their sightlines, timing your movements to the rhythm of their argument so you can memorise the chart on the barrelhead the moment Harlan looks away.

nodes.title: Chased from the Docks
nodes.brief: You observe a group of rival Wreckers' Guild members to learn their intended path, risking detection to gain a valuable map of the Low.
nodes.page:
A pebble crunches under your heel. Harlan whirls, spots you in the gloom, and draws a rusted gutting knife. "Spying for your own crew, are you?" he barks.

You bolt over the crates while rival wreckers hurl stones and curses at your back, and one jagged rock clips your temple hard enough to open a bleeding graze. The dry docks swallow you. Your head spins and you have lost time, and worse, you carry no map, so the Low ahead is entirely blind.

nodes.title: Paths of the Low
nodes.brief: You observe a group of rival Wreckers' Guild members to learn their intended path, risking detection to gain a valuable map of the Low.
nodes.page:
Slipping back into the deeper shadows just as Harlan turns, you hold your breath. An argument breaks out among the rivals over a shared flask, and in their momentary distraction, you commit the final details of the route to memory.

Retreating safely to a quiet alley, you quickly sketch the vital paths onto a scrap of sailcloth using a piece of charcoal. You now possess a reliable guide through the treacherous salt-flats and sinkholes leading toward the Sunken Stair. Breathing a quiet sigh of relief, you secure the rough chart inside your coat.

nodes.title: The Mourning Believer
nodes.brief: You coax a frightened drift pilgrim out of hiding to ask about the Meridian Gear, risking their sudden panic to earn a protective bone talisman.
nodes.page:
Huddled beneath the shadow of a stranded ferry, a figure wrapped in tattered, salt-stained kelp rocks back and forth. It is a Drift Pilgrim, one of the devoted who mourn the retreating sea. He clutches something tightly to his chest, muttering prayers to the dry wind.

You approach slowly, palms open to show you mean no harm. The pilgrims know the deep lore of the waters, and this one might possess knowledge of the Meridian Gear or the path to the Sunken Stair. However, they are a skittish sort, their minds often frayed by the sudden vanishing of their god. You will need a gentle touch.

nodes.title: Trembling Faith
nodes.brief: You coax a frightened drift pilgrim out of hiding to ask about the Meridian Gear, risking their sudden panic to earn a protective bone talisman.
nodes.page:
Hearing your footsteps, the pilgrim flinches, pulling his kelp mantle tighter around his thin shoulders. His eyes are wide and frantic, darting toward the open expanse of the Low. "The breath is gone," he whispers hoarsely, his voice trembling. "The great lung has collapsed."

You crouch at a respectful distance, speaking in low, soothing tones. You ask him about the great mechanism, the Gear that controls the waters. He whimpers, shaking his head violently, clearly terrified of the ancient Tidewarden machinery. You must find the right words to calm his religious panic and draw the truth from his rambling sorrow.

nodes.title: Heresy and Hope
nodes.brief: You coax a frightened drift pilgrim out of hiding to ask about the Meridian Gear, risking their sudden panic to earn a protective bone talisman.
nodes.page:
Carefully measuring your tone, you speak of the sea returning, of restoring the balance through the Meridian Gear. The pilgrim's eyes fix on yours, filled with a volatile mix of hope and absolute terror. He clutches a carved piece of whalebone in his trembling hands, a sacred ward.

"To touch the Gear is heresy," he stammers, rising to his knees. He looks ready to bolt or perhaps strike out in a frenzy of religious fervour. You must guide the conversation with precision, easing his frantic mind before he erupts into a panicked shout that will draw unwanted attention from the town guards or rival wreckers.

nodes.title: A Shriek in the Harbour
nodes.brief: You coax a frightened drift pilgrim out of hiding to ask about the Meridian Gear, risking their sudden panic to earn a protective bone talisman.
nodes.page:
Before you can finish your sentence, the pilgrim lets out a piercing mournful wail. "Blasphemy!" he shrieks, and a handful of coarse salt hits your eyes.

You stagger backwards, blinded and cursing. You claw the grit from your vision, and by the time tears clear the pain the pilgrim has vanished into the maze of stranded boats and left you with red aching eyes. Hostile stares from nearby scavengers mark you as a troublemaker. You have gained no answers. Only a persistent ache remains under the glare of the seabed.

nodes.title: A Pilgrim's Ward
nodes.brief: You coax a frightened drift pilgrim out of hiding to ask about the Meridian Gear, risking their sudden panic to earn a protective bone talisman.
nodes.page:
You let the pilgrim's shriek die in the damp air of the cliffs. His panic passes. He stands shivering and repentant, murmuring apologies to the absent sea, clawing at his kelp mantle. For your patience he presses a small cold object into your palm, then scuttles away toward the deeper shadows of the rocks.

It is a bleached piece of spine, carved with the symbol of an unfurling wave - a ward against the wrath of the drowned. You tuck the charm into your coat and turn back to the cliff-town, where the water used to be.

nodes.title: Stepping Onto The Low
nodes.brief: Leaving the shadow of the cliff behind, you step onto the endless salt-flats of the Low to begin your search for the missing lighthouse keeper.
nodes.page:
Turning away from the comforting gloom of Gullmouth's sheer stone, you cross the threshold of the known world. Beneath your boots, the ground crunches - a thick crust of white salt stretching out to the bruised horizon where the ocean should be. This is the Low, the naked seabed exposed by the great retreat. A grim landscape of marooned wrecks, jutting whale ribs, and shimmering sinkholes lies waiting under the harsh sun.

Somewhere out there in this vast, desiccated wasteland, Orsolya Venn is searching for the Sunken Stair and the jammed mechanism of the Meridian Gear. The wind howls across the flats, carrying the scent of rotting kelp and dried brine. You pull your collar high against the chill. There is no map for a world turned inside out, only the distant, dark shapes of scavenger camps and the looming silhouettes of coral spires. With every step away from the cliff-town, the reality of the missing sea settles heavier upon your shoulders.

nodes.title: A Precious Source of Light
nodes.brief: You dismantle a heavy brass lantern to extract its precious oil, risking a spill to secure a vital light source for the dark days ahead.
nodes.page: Carefully, you wedge your blade under the tarnished rim of the heavy brass lantern. It is a beautiful old piece of salvage, likely stripped from a nobleman's drowned yacht, but you have no need for decorative metal right now. You need the dark, viscous fuel sloshing in its belly. The hinges are rusted shut with thick green verdigris, requiring a delicate, steady hand to pry open without tipping the reservoir. The subterranean depths beneath the Sunken Stair will be pitch black, and the shadows of the Low are already lengthening. Holding your breath, you prepare to work the stubborn clasp free, hoping to decant the precious oil into your own flask before it can seep into the floorboards.

nodes.title: The Rusted Spyglass
nodes.brief: You try to repair a rusted spyglass found on the balcony, risking cutting your hands to gain a valuable tool for spotting distant scavengers.
nodes.page: Tarnished brass and cracked leather make up the ruined spyglass abandoned on the lighthouse balcony. It is jammed shut. The extending barrels have fused from years of salt spray and neglect. On the Low, a scavenger without a way to spot rivals or landmarks might as well be blind, so a broken instrument like this is still a prize if you can force it to work. Where the housing has split, the metal edges are jagged enough to open your palms if your grip slips. You plant your boots wide and take a firm hold on both ends. Break the seal of rust and the lenses inside might still be intact.

exits.label: Attempt to pry open the spyglass

nodes.title: A Dry Harbour Morning
nodes.brief: You wake in Gullmouth to a silent, dry harbour and discover Orsolya's sealed letter warning that the Meridian Gear has jammed beneath the Sunken Stair.
nodes.page:
Silence is the first thing that wakes you. The rhythmic, thunderous crash of waves against the cliffs of Gullmouth has vanished, replaced by an eerie, hollow quiet. Pushing yourself up from your cot, you look out the window and freeze. The harbour is entirely dry. Fishing smacks and smuggler galleons list pathetically in the mud, stranded amidst a vast, steaming expanse of exposed seabed stretching to the horizon.

On your washstand lies a thick envelope, sealed with the deep blue wax of the lighthouse keeper. Breaking it open, you recognise Orsolya's hurried scrawl. She writes that the Meridian Gear - the great engine of the old Tidewardens - has jammed far beneath the Sunken Stair. The sea has not merely retreated; it is locked out. Whoever turns the ancient wheel will dictate the shape of the returning waters. She has gone ahead, urging you to follow. The fate of the Wrack Coast now rests entirely on who controls the tide.

nodes.title: The Stranded Basin
nodes.brief: Gullmouth Harbour: The stranded docks are chaotic as rival wrecker crews argue over the exposed seabed and scavenge whatever they can reach first.
nodes.page:
Barnacle-crusted keels list at sickening angles in the dried silt of Gullmouth Harbour, where the salt-stench of dead weed and black mud clings to the wool of your coat. Shouts echo off the timber pilings as rival wreckers claw through the weed-matted troughs of the seabed, iron bars clinking against stranded anchors and waterlogged chests. Down among the tilted hulls and weeping brine-pipes, every man and his cousin looks for an edge before the tide clock turns its iron tooth.

Scraps of copper and heavy oak timbers lie waiting for the bold or the desperate, half-buried in the muck where the gulls have given up screeching and taken to pacing the dried mud.

exits.label: Face down the snarling rival crew blocking the fishing skiff
Rig a tackle-block to patch the hanging hull before the timber splits
Shoulder through the swollen cedar door of the abandoned bait-shack
Haggle with the mud-stuck ferryman for his survey of the sinkholes
Work a stubborn skeleton key into the harbourmaster office lock
Enter the smoky hall of the Wreckers Guild to press your claim

nodes.title: Claiming The Stranded Trawler
nodes.brief: You confront a rival crew claiming a stranded fishing boat, holding your nerve to intimidate them into backing down and securing a sturdy grappling hook.
nodes.page: Three burly scavengers from the Bilge-Rat crew are already swarming over the hull of a stranded trawler, prying at the valuable brass fittings with crowbars. Looped securely over the prow is a heavy iron grappling hook attached to a thick coil of hemp - a perfect tool for navigating the vertical drops of the exposed sinkholes out on the Low. You need that rope. Striding purposefully across the sucking mud, you call out a sharp challenge, demanding they hand over the gear. The largest of the three pauses, wiping a filthy hand across his jaw, and raises his iron bar in a silent threat. If you flinch now, they will fall upon you like starved gulls. You must stand your ground and make them believe you are the predator here.

nodes.title: A Test of Nerve
nodes.brief: You confront a rival crew claiming a stranded fishing boat, holding your nerve to intimidate them into backing down and securing a sturdy grappling hook.
nodes.page: Meeting the gaze of the lead scavenger, you square your shoulders and drop your hand to the heavy iron hook at your belt. You do not blink. You do not speak again. You simply let the cold, flat deadliness of your stare do the talking. The harbour is a brutal place, and blood in the mud is a daily occurrence, but these vultures are opportunists, not hardened killers. You walk slowly toward the hull of the trawler, putting yourself well within striking distance of the crowbar, daring him with your silence to take the swing. The wind whistling through the dry masts above is the only sound as the tension stretches to a breaking point.

nodes.title: Bruised Ribs and Pride
nodes.brief: You confront a rival crew claiming a stranded fishing boat, holding your nerve to intimidate them into backing down and securing a sturdy grappling hook.
nodes.page: Hesitation betrays you. The moment your eyes flick toward the crowbar in the scavenger's grip, he smells your uncertainty. With a jeering laugh he swings the iron bar in a vicious arc, catches you hard across the ribs, and pain explodes through your side while breath leaves you and you stumble backward into the foul-smelling muck. The crew mocks you. You scramble to your feet, coughing and clutching your bruised chest. Face is lost here. Against three armed rivals with a compromised stance you back away and leave them to their prize, and the pain in your ribs will dog you for days and sap your strength.

exits.label: Limp back to the main harbour

nodes.title: Yielding to the Predator
nodes.brief: You confront a rival crew claiming a stranded fishing boat, holding your nerve to intimidate them into backing down and securing a sturdy grappling hook.
nodes.page: Grumbling dark curses, the leader of the scavengers finally breaks eye contact and lowers his weapon. Regardless of how close things came to violence, the sheer force of your will proves too much for their cowardly hearts. They quickly gather their pry-bars and slide down the opposite side of the hull, abandoning their claim in favour of easier pickings elsewhere in the dry harbour. You wipe mud from your cheek, step to the trawler's prow, and unhook the iron grapple. The thick hemp rope is dry and perfectly coiled. Hauling it over your shoulder, you feel significantly more prepared to descend into the treacherous depths of the Low.

nodes.title: Splintered Ribs of Wood
nodes.brief: You patch a splintered skiff that hangs uselessly from the dry pier, using clever rigging to lower it and scavenging a bundle of salt-cured rations.
nodes.page:
Salt cakes thick upon the hemp ropes as you grip the pulley, hauling your weight against the dry frame of the pier. Below, the skiff hangs suspended in the salt-blistered air, its hull scarred by a hundred bruising encounters with the reef. You need to drop it gently onto the cracked mud of the Low without snapping the remaining ribs.

Reaching into your coat, you draw a length of oiled leather twine and loop it through the tackle to slow the sudden, grinding descent. You must guide the vessel down inch by inch while the dry wind howls through the empty pilings of Gullmouth.

exits.label: Lower the skiff to the mud

nodes.title: The Rigging Holds
nodes.brief: You patch a splintered skiff that hangs uselessly from the dry pier, using clever rigging to lower it and scavenging a bundle of salt-cured rations.
nodes.page:
Heavy hemp groans beneath the strain as the wooden hull swings slightly in the coastal draft, settling closer to the grey, exposed silt of the seabed. Your fingers work swiftly through the complex knots of the tackle, adjusting the tension before the whole weight can slip and shatter against a protruding piling.

A bundle of salt-cured rations rests on the thwart inside the boat, wrapped in grease-stained canvas and smelling faintly of old brine. You secure the line to an iron bollard on the dock, preparing to descend into the hull and claim your provisions.

nodes.title: Tying the Fraying Line
nodes.brief: You patch a splintered skiff that hangs uselessly from the dry pier, using clever rigging to lower it and scavenging a bundle of salt-cured rations.
nodes.page:
Ropes dry out and turn brittle when the sea abandons its shore for three long days, and the tackle you hold is no exception. With the skiff dangling precariously above the hardened mud, you must whip the frayed strands together with swift, precise knots before the whole rig snaps under the sudden weight. A single clumsy twist will send the vessel crashing down into the rocks below, ruining your only means of crossing the Low.

Drawing a length of spare twine from your pocket, you steady your breathing against the biting wind and begin to wrap the core.

nodes.title: Snap of the Hemp
nodes.brief: You patch a splintered skiff that hangs uselessly from the dry pier, using clever rigging to lower it and scavenging a bundle of salt-cured rations.
nodes.page:
Sudden friction betrays your hurried fingers, and the hemp rope parting with a sharp crack sends the skiff plunging sideways into the dry timbers of the pier. Splintered wood explodes outward, spraying shards across the mud and tearing a jagged gash in your shoulder as you dive out of the path of the falling wreckage.

You pull yourself up from the grey silt, brushing salt from the raw, bleeding wound while your precious rations scatter into the dust. The mishap costs you both time and skin, leaving you poorer by a bundle of provisions and nursing a fresh, stinging wound.

nodes.title: Rigging the Dry Pier
nodes.brief: You patch a splintered skiff that hangs uselessly from the dry pier, using clever rigging to lower it and scavenging a bundle of salt-cured rations.
nodes.page:
Splintered pine groans under your weight as you brace against the hull of the hanging skiff, sweating despite the bitter salt chill off the empty seabed. You lash a spare winch-cable through a rusted block and tackle and swing the craft clear of the rotting timber supports without snapping the brittle stays. A canvas grease-sack tucked beneath the floorboards yields three thick slabs of salt-cured cod and a half-skin of foul-tasting vinegar water.

Hauling the prize onto the gravel embankment, you catch the eye of a passing net-mender who nods slowly at your handiwork, leaving behind a small bone needle tucked into a crack in the quay as an unspoken token of professional respect.

exits.label: Drag the skiff down toward the muddy harbour

nodes.title: Iron Against Timber
nodes.brief: You heave aside a heavy iron anchor blocking access to the old bait-shack, using sheer strength to force the door and finding a lantern.
nodes.page:
Rust has welded the heavy iron anchor to the rotting boards of the bait-shack porch, sealing the door shut against anyone seeking shelter or hidden gear. You plant your boots against the warped threshold and reach for the cold metal ring, bracing your legs for a hard heave. Gullmouth remains quiet around you, save for the distant shouting of rival crews arguing over stranded lobster pots down on the flats.

Dust flakes off the iron in orange scales as you put your back into the lift, straining to break the decades-old corrosion.

nodes.title: Heaving the Anchor
nodes.brief: You heave aside a heavy iron anchor blocking access to the old bait-shack, using sheer strength to force the door and finding a lantern.
nodes.page: The heavy iron fluke is wedged deep into the swollen timber of the shack's threshold, locked fast by layers of dried salt and ancient rust. You plant your boots firmly against the splintered floorboards, grip the cold metal ring with both hands, and lean your entire weight into the lift to wrench the obstacle free. Every muscle in your back strains against the stubborn mass as you prepare to break its grip on the door.

nodes.title: Strain and Slip
nodes.brief: You heave aside a heavy iron anchor blocking access to the old bait-shack, using sheer strength to force the door and finding a lantern.
nodes.page:
Your boots slide on a patch of encrusted salt just as you heave, throwing your weight forward against the jagged iron fluke instead of lifting it. A sharp wrench tears through your lower back, dropping you to your knees in the grit with a breathless gasp.

By the time you manage to kick the heavy anchor aside, the door is open, but the exertion has left you bruised and aching. The delay costs you precious daylight, and the lantern inside the shack proves to be cracked and dry of oil.

nodes.title: Threshold Cleared
nodes.brief: You heave aside a heavy iron anchor blocking access to the old bait-shack, using sheer strength to force the door and finding a lantern.
nodes.page:
Metal screams against dry wood as the anchor finally tears free from the swollen boards, tumbles off the porch, and sinks deep into the grey mud below. You kick the warped door inward, sending a cloud of ancient dust billowing out into the salt-laden air of the cliff-town.

Just inside the threshold, a brass-hooded lantern sits on a low bench, glass intact and reservoir still half-full of clean whale oil. You pick it up, testing its weight, and slip it onto your belt as a reliable companion for the dark miles ahead.

nodes.title: The Ferryman of the Mud
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the ferryman who sits in his boat upon the mud, staring down his demands to gain a rusted map of the sinkholes.
nodes.page:
Stagnant river-stench rises from the gray silt where the ferryman rests his bottom on the thwart, his long ash pole jammed uselessly deep into the dry riverbed like a dead tree. He refuses to meet your gaze, counting greasy copper coins over and over in his cracked palm while muttering complaints about the lack of current and the insolence of eels. You lean your forearm against his gunwale, matching his stubborn silence until the rhythmic clicking of his copper tokens finally stumbles and stops.

Without a word, he slides a stiff sheet of beaten copper across the damp bench, its surface etched with the treacherous maze of sinkholes that now scar the upper seabed.

exits.label: Follow the etched copper down the slope

nodes.title: Tracing the Drowned Channels
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the ferryman who sits in his boat upon the mud, staring down his demands to gain a rusted map of the sinkholes.
nodes.page:
Cold brine flakes off the copper sheet as your thumb traces the jagged scratches marking where the old harbor channel used to run before the sea withdrew. Every line represents a fathom of treacherous mud where the silt crusts over deep brine-pits waiting to swallow an unwary scavenger whole. You fold the heavy metal sheet into your coat pocket, feeling its sharp corner press against your ribs with every stride you take toward the drop-off.

Down below, the vast gray expanse of the Low stretches toward the horizon under a pale, greasy sky, littered with the black ribs of stranded brigs and forgotten wharves.

exits.label: Descend the cliff path toward the open seabed

nodes.title: Meeting the Ferryman's Gaze
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the ferryman who sits in his boat upon the mud, staring down his demands to gain a rusted map of the sinkholes.
nodes.page:
The ferryman is an old fixture of Gullmouth who has ferried the dead and the desperate across the channel for forty years, and he knows how to break a younger wrecker's nerve with a single flat stare. He demands twice your remaining coin for a scrap of paper showing where the sinkholes hide beneath the salt-crust of the Low.

You stand your ground on the dry mud beside his stranded boat, locking your eyes onto his without flinching, refusing to show the desperation gnawing at your ribs.

nodes.title: The Price of Mud
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the ferryman who sits in his boat upon the mud, staring down his demands to gain a rusted map of the sinkholes.
nodes.page: The ferryman does not blink as he names a price that leaves your pockets stinging with loss and your skin crawling with salt-rash. When you finally snatch the rusted copper map from his grease-stained palm, a jagged edge of the metal slices deep into the meat of your thumb, drawing thick, dark blood that immediately crusts over with grey rime. The delay has cost you half your morning and a good portion of your remaining water skin, leaving your throat dry and your temper short as the salt-stiffened mud sucks at your boots.

exits.label: Climb back up to the cliff-top

nodes.title: The Ferryman's Price
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the ferryman who sits in his boat upon the mud, staring down his demands to gain a rusted map of the sinkholes.
nodes.page:
Bargaining with the old man requires a steady tongue and a willingness to match his stubborn silence. You lean against the wet timber of the gunwale, offering a small twist of cured tobacco and a sharp knife in exchange for his accumulated wisdom of the silt-channels. He turns the blade over in his palm, testing its edge against a horny thumb, before spitting a brown stream into the gray muck. With a grunt, he slides a grease-stained, stiffened goatskin map across the thwart. It details the treacherous sinkholes and hidden drops where careless scavengers lose their boots to the suction.

You pocket the chart, knowing the paths it reveals will keep your feet out of the suffocating mire.

exits.label: Take the map and move on

nodes.title: Office of Tides
nodes.brief: You pick the rusted lock on the harbourmaster's abandoned office, relying on careful hands to disarm a simple trap and claiming a stash of coin.
nodes.page: Until you wedge a crowbar into the swollen frame and throw your body against the iron, the oak door of the harbourmaster's abandoned office resists your tug. Inside, the air smells of moldering ledgers and stagnant vinegar, untouched since the water vanished from the sills. You kneel before the brass-bound strongbox set into the floorboards, pulling a set of fine wire picks from your belt. Your fingers work by feel alone, listening for the faint clicks of the internal levers as a tripwire of thin copper wire waits just above the keyhole. You ease the tension bar, nudge the final tumbler aside, and lift the heavy iron lid. A tidy stack of silver coins rests within the velvet-lined well.

nodes.title: The Harbor Office
nodes.brief: You pick the rusted lock on the harbourmaster's abandoned office, relying on careful hands to disarm a simple trap and claiming a stash of coin.
nodes.page: Sunlight cuts through the grimy salt-crusted windows of the harbourmaster's abandoned office, illuminating dust motes dancing above scattered papers. You step carefully over a discarded ledger, keeping your eyes on the open strongbox where the silver coins gleam in the dim light. Reaching down, you gather the metal pieces into a leather pouch; their pleasant clink breaks the hush of the stranded waterfront. The room holds nothing else of immediate value, save for a brass spyglass mounted on a tripod facing the empty bay. You take a final look across the dry silt before turning your back on the quiet desk.

nodes.title: Picking the Lock
nodes.brief: You pick the rusted lock on the harbourmaster's abandoned office, relying on careful hands to disarm a simple trap and claiming a stash of coin.
nodes.page: Crouched in the harbourmaster's abandoned office, you study the brass works of the floor safe. A hair-thin wire runs from the lock tumbler to a loaded spring-gun set into the wainscoting. You slide your thinnest pick into the keyhole and hold your breath while sweat runs into your eyes. Each shift of metal balances tumbler tension against the hidden trigger. Your pulse knocks in your ears as you press the final internal tooth and feel for whether the trap will hold or spring.

check.label: Disarm the trap and pick the lock

nodes.title: A Slip of the Pick
nodes.brief: You pick the rusted lock on the harbourmaster's abandoned office, relying on careful hands to disarm a simple trap and claiming a stash of coin.
nodes.page: A sudden metallic snap echoes through the empty office as the tripwire catches your sleeve, triggering a small poisoned dart that grazes your forearm. You hiss in pain, yanking your hand back just as the dart embeds itself deep into the wooden wainscoting behind you. Blackened venom begins to burn through your blood, so you bind the raw scratch tight with a strip of rag from your coat. The strongbox remains sealed, mocking your haste, and the lost time leaves your nerves frayed and your supplies lighter. You stagger out into the salt-air, carrying a dull ache and a hard lesson about old harbor traps.

nodes.title: Spoils of the Office
nodes.brief: You pick the rusted lock on the harbourmaster's abandoned office, relying on careful hands to disarm a simple trap and claiming a stash of coin.
nodes.page: Working with patient care, you bypass the concealed tripwire and trip the internal levers with a satisfying double click. On rusted hinges the iron lid pops upward, releasing a puff of stale air and revealing a neat leather pouch of silver coins. You slip the purse into your coat, feeling its reassuring weight against your ribs as you survey the quiet, abandoned room. The risk was high, but the reward ensures you can buy whatever provisions or gear you need before venturing out onto the dried seabed. Prize secured, you check the door once more and slip back out into the salty breeze.

nodes.title: The Guildmaster's Ledger
nodes.brief: You enter the Wreckers' Guild to formally register your salvage claim for the deep basin, where the guildmaster demands proof of your intentions.
nodes.page: Heavy oak doors swing inward to the Wreckers' Guild, where peat smoke hangs thick above scarred tables and men smell of old brine and cheap ale. You push through the crowd to the high counter of driftwood where the guildmaster sits, his fingers stained black with ink and tar. He looks you over with milky eyes, demanding to know what right you have to claim the deep basin where Orsolya vanished. You slap your salvaged papers onto the scarred wood, stating your intentions with a steady voice that brooks no argument from the seated elders. He grunts, dipping his quill into a horn of ink to log your name among the authorized salvage crews of Gullmouth.

nodes.title: Smoke and Rumours
nodes.brief: The Wreckers' Guild: The smoky guildhall is filled with grim scavengers placing wagers on what lies beneath the mud, offering you a chance to prepare.
nodes.page: Low murmurs and the clink of horn mugs fill the smoky guildhall of Gullmouth as scavengers lay fat wagers on what lies exposed beneath the vanished sea. Shadows stretch long across the floorboards from the hearth fire, where weathered men argue over tide charts and the strange silence of the horizon. You stand near the center of the room, weighing your options as various factions and desperate locals eye your boots with cautious interest. Every corner offers a different path into the dry abyss, whether through brawn, quick wits, or quiet bargains with the townsfolk. The air tastes of dried kelp and impending trouble.

exits.label: Haul water crates from the cellar
Face the Customs-Priest at the gates

nodes.title: Staring Down the Brineholder
nodes.brief: You stare down a bragging Brineholder agent making offers to the locals, refusing to blink and extracting a valuable secret about the patrol routes.
nodes.page: A slick Brineholder agent in an immaculate salt-silk coat leans against a pillar, tossing silver coins in the air and mocking the ruined harbor. You step directly into his path, planting your boots firmly on the floorboards and fixing him with a cold, unblinking stare that wipes the smirk from his face. The surrounding conversations die down as the two of you lock eyes, neither man willing to show weakness in front of the guild. Under the relentless pressure of your gaze, the agent shifts uncomfortably and lets slip the exact departure times and patrol routes of the Brineholder water-wagons heading out onto the Low. You commit every detail to memory before turning away with a dry smile.

nodes.title: The Staring Match
nodes.brief: You stare down a bragging Brineholder agent making offers to the locals, refusing to blink and extracting a valuable secret about the patrol routes.
nodes.page: You square your shoulders opposite the wealthy Brineholder agent, refusing to drop your gaze as he tries to stare you down with arrogant condescension. The tavern grows dead silent, every wrecker watching to see whose nerve breaks first against the polished outsider. Sweat beads on your forehead, but you keep your breathing even, matching his haughty grin with a flat, dangerous expression born of the salt-cliffs. The tension stretches thin as gut-string, and you must hold your ground against his psychological games before he yields the information you need.

nodes.title: Breaking Gaze
nodes.brief: You stare down a bragging Brineholder agent making offers to the locals, refusing to blink and extracting a valuable secret about the patrol routes.
nodes.page: A sudden twitch in your eye betrays your concentration, and the Brineholder agent lets out a sharp, mocking laugh that bangs off the timber walls. You blink hard. The spell breaks and you flush with anger as the tavern resumes its noisy chatter around you. The agent pockets his silver with a sneer, refuses to share anything useful, and leaves you with a headache and bruised pride. The failure costs you precious time and sets your nerves on edge among the watchful locals. You pull back from the table, already hunting another way to learn what the wealthy interlopers are planning.

nodes.title: The Agent's Slip
nodes.brief: You stare down a bragging Brineholder agent making offers to the locals, refusing to blink and extracting a valuable secret about the patrol routes.
nodes.page: Unable to break your iron stare, the Brineholder agent finally averts his eyes with a muttered curse, tossing a crumpled parchment onto the sticky table in frustration. You snatch it up before he can snatch it back, seeing the detailed patrol schedules and guard rotations for the deep seabed routes. It is a vital piece of leverage that will let you slip past their checkpoints without paying their exorbitant tolls. You tuck the paper safely inside your jacket, leaving the defeated agent to nurse his bruised ego in the corner.

nodes.title: Blood on the Net
nodes.brief: You intervene in a knife-point argument between two net-menders, keeping calm to defuse the tension and earning the loyalty of a tough local guide.
nodes.page:
Voices crackle like dried kelp beneath the wooden docks where the drying frames cast long, skeletal shadows. Two net-menders stand chest-to-chest, iron fish-knives drawn and glinting with pale salt-crust under the grey Gullmouth sky. Passers-by edge away and mutter into woolen collars. The dispute is theirs alone now. You step between them with slow palms held open and watch the twitch of tendon and knuckle as razor edges hover inches from wet wool.

A scarred local guide named Bran leans against a salt-cured piling with a coil of hemp over his shoulder. He narrows his eyes. Your ground holds while the steel stays high.

nodes.title: The Blade's Edge
nodes.brief: You intervene in a knife-point argument between two net-menders, keeping calm to defuse the tension and earning the loyalty of a tough local guide.
nodes.page: Shrill curses bounce off the salt-limed stones of the net-shed as two grizzled net-menders square off, rusted fish-knives flashing in the damp air. Their frayed tempers threaten to draw a blood-feud right in the heart of Gullmouth when the town can least afford fracture. Stepping directly between the swinging blades, you keep your breathing even and your palms open, fixing the louder antagonist with a steady, unblinking glare that demands quiet. A heavy silence falls over the surrounding onlookers as you reach out an unhurried hand toward the nearest razor-sharp edge.

nodes.title: A Slip in the Salt
nodes.brief: You intervene in a knife-point argument between two net-menders, keeping calm to defuse the tension and earning the loyalty of a tough local guide.
nodes.page: Steel catches the dreary grey light, and a sudden, jagged jerk from the older mender bypasses your defences entirely, slicing a deep, burning furrow across your forearm before you can pin his wrist. Blood wells instantly, hot and bright against the brine-caked wool of your sleeve, while the crowd gasps and surges backward in alarm. You stagger against a stack of rotting hemp nets and clutch the cut as the combatants break apart, thoroughly shamed by your sudden spilling of blood. The cost is heavy in both torn flesh and lost time, leaving you throbbing and breathless as you bind the tear with a dirty rag.

exits.label: Bind your bleeding arm and push onward

nodes.title: The Net-Menders' Dispute
nodes.brief: You intervene in a knife-point argument between two net-menders, keeping calm to defuse the tension and earning the loyalty of a tough local guide.
nodes.page: Cold brine drips from the rafters as the rusted fish-hook flashes between the two bickering net-menders, their hoarse voices rising above the scrape of mending needles against stone. You step between the squared shoulders without drawing steel, speaking in the quiet, level tone of someone who has hauled bodies from the surf before. Silence settles over the greasy flagstones as the taller of the two lowers his blade with a muttered apology, recognizing the authority of a seasoned scavenger. The younger mender presses a notched bone whistle into your palm and swears to answer whenever you blow it against the damp harbor mists.

exits.label: Seek the warmth of the guildhall

nodes.title: The Guildmaster's Table
nodes.brief: You challenge the guildmaster's champion to an arm-wrestling contest, putting your back into the strain to win a coil of high-quality climbing rope.
nodes.page: Thick oak groans beneath the weight of two straining forearms as the guildmaster's champion grins across the grease-stained tavern table, his muscles bunched like oiled cables. You lock your fingers into his massive grip, planting your boots firmly against the uneven floorboards while the smoky taproom falls silent around the wager. Every eye in Gullmouth watches the sweat bead on your forehead as you throw your weight behind the push, fighting inch by grueling inch against an adversary who has broken better wreckers than you. The contest leaves your arm trembling and your lungs burning with stale ale and salt-dust, but victory remains within your desperate grasp as you shove his knuckles down toward the scarred wood.

exits.label: Claim your prize from the tavern keeper

nodes.title: Coils of Hemp
nodes.brief: You challenge the guildmaster's champion to an arm-wrestling contest, putting your back into the strain to win a coil of high-quality climbing rope.
nodes.page: Coarse hemp rope, tightly braided and dripping with protective pitch, lands with a satisfying thud on the tavern bench before you. The defeated champion rubs his reddened wrist with a wry grimace, tossing you a nod of grudging respect that earns the silent approval of the surrounding scavengers. Slinging the heavy coil over your bruised shoulder, you turn your back on the cheering taproom and step out into the damp, sea-scented gloom of the cliff-town. The endless grey expanse of the Low beckons from beyond the harbour wall, waiting for those prepared to descend its treacherous slopes.

exits.label: Step out toward the naked seabed

nodes.title: Bending the Iron Arm
nodes.brief: You challenge the guildmaster's champion to an arm-wrestling contest, putting your back into the strain to win a coil of high-quality climbing rope.
nodes.page: Oak splinters groan beneath your elbow as you lock palms with the guildmaster's champion across the scarred tavern table, your forearm trembling under the weight of his granite-hard muscles. Blue veins bulge against your skin while the crowd of salt-cured wreckers leans in close, smelling of stale ale and dried weed as they roar their wagers into the smoky air. You grind your teeth, plant your boots firmly into the damp rushes, and throw every ounce of your shoulder strength into turning his knuckles back toward the wood.

nodes.title: Broken Sinews
nodes.brief: You challenge the guildmaster's champion to an arm-wrestling contest, putting your back into the strain to win a coil of high-quality climbing rope.
nodes.page: A sickening pop jumps through your shoulder joint as the champion surges up with brute force. Your leverage breaks. Your knuckles slam the splintered oak. Pain flares hot down your arm; your fingers go numb, and the defeat sticks. You stumble back from the table, clutching your wrist, while the onlookers jeer and scoop their winning copper coins off the bar. Strength and standing among the guild both take the hit. You nurse the arm in the shadows of the smoky hall.

exits.label: Retreat to lick your wounds in silence

nodes.title: Winning the Strong Cord
nodes.brief: You challenge the guildmaster's champion to an arm-wrestling contest, putting your back into the strain to win a coil of high-quality climbing rope.
nodes.page: Sweat stings your eyes as the champion's knuckles finally hit the notched grain of the oak table with a resounding thack, the tavern erupting into boisterous curses and approving cheers. You shake out your aching arm and take the coil of tarred hemp rope tossed across the ale-rings with a dry nod of acknowledgment. The prize is stiff and salt-cured, perfect for dropping into the abyss of the seabed or hauling crates from drowned cellars, and it rides your shoulder as you step back out into the salty drizzle.

nodes.title: Hauling the Hidden Cask
nodes.brief: You haul a crate of smuggled fresh water from the cellar, proving your worth through brute labour to receive a rare talisman of safe passage.
nodes.page:
Cool moisture seeps through the rotting staves of the oak cask as you hoist it up the damp stone steps of the cellar, and your boots slip on the slimy moss. Smuggled fresh water is the rarest currency left in Gullmouth. Every drop saved from the Brineholders' monopoly is worth a king's ransom among the net-menders.

The cask hits the flagged floor. You wipe sweat from your brow and catch the approving eye of the cellar master. From his grease-stained coat he draws a small, cold piece of hammered tin and places it in your hand.

exits.label: Leave the damp cellar with your token

nodes.title: Lifting the Dead Weight
nodes.brief: You haul a crate of smuggled fresh water from the cellar, proving your worth through brute labour to receive a rare talisman of safe passage.
nodes.page: Bracing your knees against the damp masonry of the cellar wall, you slide your arms beneath the bulging belly of the massive water cask and prepare to heave. The wood is slick with condensation, and the dead weight threatens to tear the muscles right out of your lower back as you strain upward against the choking dark. Every breath tastes of stagnant lime and ancient mud while you summon every last scrap of strength to hoist the cargo clear of the stone floor.

nodes.title: A Crushing Slip
nodes.brief: You haul a crate of smuggled fresh water from the cellar, proving your worth through brute labour to receive a rare talisman of safe passage.
nodes.page: The heavy cask shifts treacherously at the apex of the lift, its sodden weight slipping from your numb fingers and crashing back down onto your boot with a bone-jarring thud. Agony shoots up your shin, leaving you gasping for air in the cramped, freezing dark of the cellar while precious fresh water leaks through a newly cracked stave. You limp out into the dim light of the alley a few minutes later, nursing a swollen foot and a bruised ego while cursing your failing grip.

exits.label: Hobble away from the ruined cellar

nodes.title: Hauling the Water Crate
nodes.brief: You haul a crate of smuggled fresh water from the cellar, proving your worth through brute labour to receive a rare talisman of safe passage.
nodes.page: Muscles burn and your boots slip slightly on the slimy cellar moss as you heave the heavy water crate up the damp stone steps, your breath coming in ragged gasps against the chill air. The damp staves are slick with condensation, but you brace your back against the masonry and lift until your thighs ache and the precious cargo clears the threshold. Impressed by your stubborn endurance, the old cellar-keeper presses a tarnished lead pendant into your palm, muttering a brief coastal blessing for safe passage across the exposed mud flats.

nodes.title: The Customs-Priest at the Gate
nodes.brief: The skeletal Customs-Priest intercepts you at the town gates, demanding a tithe for the absent sea before allowing you to step onto the crusting salt-flats.
nodes.page:
Iron chains drag across the dry cobbles of the sea-gate where the grey water used to lap against the foundation stones. Father Vane stands wrapped in salt-stiffened robes that smell of dead kelp and stale vinegar, his eye sockets hollow beneath a narrow bronze mitre. He blocks the exit with a brass ledger held in skin-tight fingers, demanding the dead-water tax before any living soul sets foot upon the newly exposed seabed. His voice sounds like dry reeds scraping in a winter gale as he insists that the absence of the tide remains taxable under ancient maritime charter.

You press past his outstretched arm, ignoring the low hum of his acolytes chanting hymns to the departed salt, and step out onto the grey, sun-baked expanse of the Low.

exits.label: Step past the toll-gate onto the salt flats

nodes.title: The Crusting Salt-Flats
nodes.brief: The Crusting Salt-flats: The mud is rapidly hardening under the strange sun, hiding treacherous sinkholes and half-buried treasures waiting to be claimed.
nodes.page: Miles of grey, baking mud stretch toward a bleached horizon where the seabed has dried into jagged ridges and treacherous hollows. The morning sun beats down without the cooling breath of the missing tide, baking the exposed silt into a crust that hides bottomless pockets of black muck beneath. Strange shapes jut from the hardened sediment - the ribs of ribs and hulls of long-forgotten craft that now lie stranded in the open air. In the distance, figures move like scavengers across a massive carcass, while closer at hand, the salt crust crackles underfoot with every cautious step you take into the vast unknown.

exits.label: Search the muddy shallows for buried salvage
Balance along the narrow ridge of dried silt
Lash together a makeshift driftwood sledge
Pick through the wake of the frantic pilgrims
Approach the pawn-widow near the stranded hull

nodes.title: Sunken Riches in the Muck
nodes.brief: You drag a waterlogged chest from a collapsing mud pit, using your strength to pull it free before it sinks and claiming the silver within.
nodes.page: Dark water pools sluggishly around the corners of a sunken timber frame, where the seabed has given way under the unaccustomed heat. Thick, foul-smelling silt clings to your shins as you wade into the depression and dig into the mud for the iron-bound edges of a chest. The salt-crrusted lid resists your initial pull, wedged firmly against a bed of waterlogged stones and broken pottery. You wedge your fingers beneath the rusted clasp and plant your heels in the hardening silt to begin the hard pull of extraction.

exits.label: Heave the chest clear of the sucking mire

nodes.title: Hauling the Heavy Chest
nodes.brief: You drag a waterlogged chest from a collapsing mud pit, using your strength to pull it free before it sinks and claiming the silver within.
nodes.page: Strain pulls hard against your shoulders and back as you lean into the effort, muscles trembling under the dead weight of the sunken burden. The mire surrenders inch by inch, sucking at the timber sides with a wet, gasping sound like lungs drawing air after a drowning. Saltwater drips from the iron straps as the box finally breaks free of the suction, sliding up onto the firmer crust of the salt-flat with a dull, echoing thud. You catch your breath, wiping stinging sweat from your forehead, and flip the rusted latch to see what the retreating sea has left behind.

exits.label: Pocket the heavy silver coins inside

nodes.title: Breaking the Silt's Grasp
nodes.brief: You drag a waterlogged chest from a collapsing mud pit, using your strength to pull it free before it sinks and claiming the silver within.
nodes.page: Thick, suffocating mud wraps around your boots like cold fingers and tries to drag the wooden chest back down into the black depths of the pit. You plant your boots deeper into the stabilizing rocks at the edge of the collapse, gathering every ounce of strength in your frame for one final, desperate heave. The wood groans under the strain as you lock your elbows and brace your spine against the downward pull of the sinkhole, praying the rusted handles hold firm for another heartbeat.

check.label: Yank the heavy chest from the sinking mud

nodes.title: A Costly Extraction
nodes.brief: You drag a waterlogged chest from a collapsing mud pit, using your strength to pull it free before it sinks and claiming the silver within.
nodes.page: The chest slips from your sweating palms with a sharp snap of rusted iron, plunging back into the black mire and splashing foul-smelling mud across your face and chest. You stumble backward onto the hard salt crust, coughing and gasping for clean air as the suction swallows the prize out of sight. A sharp edge of buried slate catches your shin through the cloth of your trousers, leaving a hot, throbbing ache and a long, bleeding gash that will take days to heal. You pick yourself up from the dirt, poorer in both time and blood, and press on across the flats.

exits.label: Leave the sunken chest and push onward

nodes.title: The Sunken Silver
nodes.brief: You drag a waterlogged chest from a collapsing mud pit, using your strength to pull it free before it sinks and claiming the silver within.
nodes.page:
Thick gray mud cakes your knuckles as you heave the waterlogged chest from the collapsing pit, your muscles straining until the suction finally breaks with a wet, sucking gasp. Inside the salt-crusted lid lies a handful of heavy silver coins minted during the reign of the third Tidewarden, their edges worn smooth by centuries of tides.

You slip the damp currency into your coat pocket alongside a small lead token stamped with the gull-and-harpoon seal of the guild, a tangible proof of your persistence against the shifting earth of the Low.

exits.label: Search among the ribs of the ruined galleon

nodes.title: The Ridge Between Abysses
nodes.brief: You cross a narrow ridge between two yawning chasms of black mud, keeping a steady balance to reach a stranded merchant's dropped satchel of supplies.
nodes.page: A narrow spine of hard-baked silt offers the only safe passage between two yawning craters of black, bubbling sludge that drop away into darkness. The wind whistles across the flat expanse, carrying the distant scent of rotting kelp and the faint sound of iron machinery turning far below the earth. A leather satchel dangles tantalizingly from the broken spar of a stranded merchant skiff wedged on the far side of the chasm. Every step along the razor-thin ridge requires absolute focus, as the crust beneath your soles crumbles and drifts away into the void with every movement.

exits.label: Walk the narrow ridge to reach the satchel

nodes.title: Crossing the Razor Ridge
nodes.brief: You cross a narrow ridge between two yawning chasms of black mud, keeping a steady balance to reach a stranded merchant's dropped satchel of supplies.
nodes.page: The wind hits your chest like a solid wall, threatening to tip your balance over the edge of the crumbling mud ridge and into the black mire below. You freeze mid-stride, arms held wide to catch the shifting air currents, fixing your eyes entirely on the weathered leather satchel swaying just yards ahead. Every muscle in your body locks tight as a fresh tremor shakes the salt-flats, threatening to break the fragile bridge of earth beneath your boots into dust.

check.label: Keep your balance across the chasm ridge

nodes.title: A Slips on the Edge
nodes.brief: You cross a narrow ridge between two yawning chasms of black mud, keeping a steady balance to reach a stranded merchant's dropped satchel of supplies.
nodes.page: A brittle shelf of salt collapses beneath your left boot without warning, sending a shower of grey dust rattling down into the dark abyss below. You throw your weight backward with a sharp gasp, catching your ribs hard against the jagged spine of the ridge as the wind tries to peel you from the rock. Your supplies rattle loose within your pack, and a leather flask of precious fresh water slips from its lashings, tumbling silently into the depths of the mire. Bruised and shaken, you crawl the final few yards on your hands and knees until you reach the safety of solid ground.

exits.label: Gather your breath and continue onward

nodes.title: Across the Ridge
nodes.brief: You cross a narrow ridge between two yawning chasms of black mud, keeping a steady balance to reach a stranded merchant's dropped satchel of supplies.
nodes.page:
Narrow and treacherous, the ridge of dried silt offers barely enough space for the soles of your boots as you edge across the yawning chasms of black mud, arms held wide to catch any stray gust of salt-laden wind. A few paces further, half-buried in the hardening crust, rests a leather merchant satchel dropped in some forgotten panic.

You pull the stiff straps free from the grip of the drying mire, finding dried salt-fish and a tightly stoppered flask of clean well-water intact within the pouch, untouched by the brackish rot of the seabed.

exits.label: Head back toward the hardening salt-flats

nodes.title: Driftwood Sledge Construction
nodes.brief: You construct a makeshift sledge from driftwood planks, lashing the wood together to safely cross a patch of soft silt and recover an ivory spyglass.
nodes.page: Splintered ribs of a long-dead ketch provide the sturdy spars you need, and you drag them across the crusting silt until you reach the edge of the trembling grey quagmire.
