nodes.page: Gullmouth wakes to the sound of water crashing against its stone quays once more, foaming white and thick with weed and small, glittering shells that have not seen the light for a hundred years. The stranded boats in the basin lift and tug at their dry ropes with a joyous, wooden groaning, while net-menders and weeping tavern-keepers crowd the wet cobbles to dip their bare hands into the cold brine. Orsolya is gone from the Sunken Stair, leaving behind only her iron-tipped walking staff propped against the lighthouse door and a single wet footprint on the threshold. Alone on the winding cliff path, you take the salt spray on your cheeks and carry the tide clock's truth with you.

exits.label: Walk down to the wet shore

nodes.title: The Last Tide
nodes.brief: Ending "Orsolya's Way"
nodes.page: Orsolya Venn was right about water, though she did not live to see the grey silt settle over her lighthouse door. You leave the salt-crusted helm of the Meridian Gear locked in its final unyielding turn. From the high stone gallery you watch the first true rollers heave themselves back against the shingle of Gullmouth, and the sea comes not roaring but with a long sliding sigh that reclaims drowned alleys and whale-bone shambles until the cliff-town floats once more on its own narrow shadow. Down in the damp dark of the stairwell the automaton-archivist folds its brass fingers and goes silent for good. Its ink has dried. There are no more charts. No secrets hide in the dry salt-pans where the world used to end. You walk back down the cliff path through a mist that tastes of cold weed and old iron, and your boots sink into familiar mud while in the tavern square the tide clock has stopped its frantic ticking with its copper hand pointed straight up at the noon that never fails. Gullmouth is rich, wet, and safe behind its breakwaters. The horizon is once more just an empty grey line where the sky meets flat indifferent water.

nodes.title: The Spoils of the Low
nodes.brief: Ending "The Wreckers' Tide"
nodes.page: With a heavy, rhythmic heaving of the great iron levers, you set the Meridian Gear to favour the Wreckers' Guild, locking the brass mechanism into a permanent, lucrative flood tide that keeps the richest wrecks forever shallow and exposed. Down on the seabed, the Brineholders' high stilted city of Saltspire is caught completely unawares as the water surges back in a chaotic, frothing torrent that swamps their lower ladders and sends their clerks scrambling for the roofs. The Gullmouth boats leap from the dry mud with a sharp crack of hemp and timber, their decks instantly slick with black kelp and bright, swirling foam. Your fellow wreckers cheer from the quays, waving iron gaffs and copper salt-scoops in the blinding afternoon glare.

exits.label: Claim the wealth of the stranded floor

nodes.title: The Wreckers' Kingdom
nodes.brief: Ending "The Wreckers' Tide"
nodes.page: Iron levers screech as your crew throws their full mass into the brass teeth of the mechanism, forcing the Meridian Gear into a permanent, greedy lock that drains the outer deeps and heaps the wealth of nations right beneath the Gullmouth docks. Salt-crusted chests of silver and ribs of ancient galleons lie open in perpetual shallow pools, ready for the mattocks and canvas sacks of the Guild. Down on the quays, the pawn-widow rings her brass bell to mark the opening of a market that will never close, trading damp silks and copperplate maps for measures of dried cod and fresh well-water. The Brineholders scream from their stilted towers out on the flats, their water-monopolies broken forever by the constant rush of your engineered tide, but no one listens to men who sell what the sea now gives away for nothing. On the wet stone of the sea-wall, spray in your teeth and a fat purse at your belt, you watch the great ships tilt against the mud in neat, orderly rows just where you told them to lie.

exits.label: Inspect the chests in the shallows

nodes.title: The Endless Harvest
nodes.brief: Ending "The Wreckers' Tide"
nodes.page: On the spoils of a controlled ocean, Gullmouth grows fat and defiant, its stone alleys choked with barrels of salt fish, strange relics from drowned cities, and chests of silver recovered from the unending shallows. The Brineholders send envoys with sealed parchment proposals and fat purses of bribes, but your crew turns them away at the cliff gate with a laugh and a handful of wet sand. You keep the tide clock locked in the Guildhouse back room, its brass fingers twitching against the glass like the legs of a drowned spider. The sea obeys your hand, rising and falling to order, but at night, when the wind howls against the slate roof, you can still hear the distant, grinding roar of the Meridian Gear waiting for someone to change their mind.

nodes.title: The Pilgrim Crown
nodes.brief: Ending "Pilgrim King"
nodes.page:
Drift Pilgrims kneel in the brine while a salt-rimed mantle settles across your shoulders, damp as wet fleece. They do not call you wrecker any longer; they name you the keeper of the receding horizon and the guardian of the sulking deep. Your boots stand ankle-deep in weed-strung foam that never stirs from its mark, forever faithful to the throne you carved out of driftwood and dried skate-skin at the water's edge. Salt crystals crust your eyelashes like cold coins, but you watch the gray line where sky and silt weld shut. Gullmouth sends its barrels of coin down the cliff road by mule-train, paying homage to the sovereign who turned the key and locked the ocean where the faithful wanted it.

Far out on the flats, the stilted skeletons of Saltspire stand silent against the glare, abandoned by their moneyed masters who have nothing left to sell. You hold the brass crank-handle of the Meridian Gear tucked inside your belt like an iron rib, cold against your skin, while the kneeling host chants old prayers to a dry and grateful sky.

nodes.title: Sovereignty of the Low
nodes.brief: Ending "Pilgrim King"
nodes.page: Night comes down over the seabed like a damp wool blanket soaked in kelp juice and old copper. Lanterns flicker along the stranded whale-market where the fish-mongers and salvage-men pay tribute in pearls and silver spoons fished from the ribs of dead galleons. You sit upon a chair constructed from the helm-wheel of an East Indiaman, your boots propped on a chest of heavy Spanish dollars that nobody dares to touch without your nod. The Drift Pilgrims light their tallow dips in long lines along the dunes, singing low, mournful choruses that drift across the mud-flats like gulls calling before a gale. No tide comes to wash away the footprints you leave in the gray silt, and no sail ever rounds the headland to dispute your crown. You are the monarch of the empty wet, ruling an empire of mud and drowned gold.

nodes.title: Kingdom of the Dry Horizon
nodes.brief: Ending "Pilgrim King"
nodes.page: Silence settles over the great Low until the only sound is the slow, dripping trickle of brine leaking from the rusted joints of the Meridian Gear far below. You have given Gullmouth its eternal feast and the pilgrims their sullen god, leaving the rest of the world to choke on dry air and memory. The sea lies tamed at your feet like a beaten hound, held in a perpetual, unmoving shallow that yields its silver without a struggle. No further storms will ever batter the cliff-town, and no stranger will ever arrive from across the water with news of a greener shore. Here you remain, king of the salt-pans and master of the locked tide, watching the gray mist swallow the last faint smudge of the horizon until nothing is left but you, the mud, and the unchanging dark.

nodes.title: Weight of the Iron
nodes.brief: Ending "Spent"
nodes.page: Your arms feel as if they have been forged from pig-iron and left in the rain to rust until every joint screams at the smallest shift of weight. The great brass levers of the Meridian Gear have left their grease burnt into your palms, dark and permanent as a smith's mark. Down in the dripping damp of the Sunken Stair, the Hollow Choir murmurs its endless, dripping liturgy from the wet walls, but their voices sound small and distant now, like water running down a drain. You have turned the world until it locked, and now there is nothing left for your hands to grip except the cold stone of the shaft and the memory of Orsolya's sealed note. The salt-crust thickens in your hair, stiffening every strand until your head feels bound in a helmet of gray shell.

exits.label: Climb back toward the upper air

nodes.title: Spent at the Root
nodes.brief: Ending "Spent"
nodes.page: Steps lead upward through the dark, but your knees refuse the climb. They tremble like old timber under a falling roof. You sink down against the damp brickwork of the Sunken Stair. The seal-oil lantern drips toward its final spark. Somewhere above, Gullmouth grows fat on the silver and salt-fish you bought with your marrow, and its taverns roar with the laughter of men who never saw the bottom of the deep. You close your eyes. Earth and locked sea press from every side, cold as wet sand stacked to a mountain. Cold creeps up through your boots until salt settles behind your tongue. The lantern gutters once more.

nodes.title: The Quiet Sand
nodes.brief: Ending "The Quiet Sand"
nodes.page: Nothing stirs on the miles of grey silt where the tide used to break against the cliffs of Gullmouth. The great iron levers of the Sunken Stair stand silent, cold with salt-frost, their teeth locked into a motionless brass eternity that neither floods nor ebbs. Down in the dry gullies, the stranded leviathan rots slowly under a grey, sunless sky, its ribs like the skeleton of an overturned cathedral filled with drifts of powdery salt. No gulls wheel overhead, and no lanterns bob along the horizon where the Brineholders once guarded their water-towers on stilts. You walk alone across the level floor of the world, your boots crunching on tiny, dead shells and the brittle remains of things that forgot how to breathe long before the old wardens laid their iron to sleep.

exits.label: Walk toward the distant grey horizon

nodes.title: Beyond the Wreck-Fields
nodes.brief: Ending "The Quiet Sand"
nodes.page: Rusted anchors and the ribs of stranded sloops rise from the dried mud like the cage-work of some monstrous beast buried by a careless tide. You pass them without a glance. Your pockets are empty of silver, and your hands are clean of brass grease for the first time since the water left the coast. A cold wind moans through the Singing Dunes away to the west and lifts gray dust into the air. In the distance the stilt-legs of Saltspire loom through the haze, their ladders dangling above the dry silt where no skiff has docked for days. The Brineholders have locked their doors and gone inland. Gulls claim the glass towers, and salt-drift wanders the steps.

exits.label: Cross the line of the old harbor

nodes.title: Leaving the Shore Behind
nodes.brief: Ending "The Quiet Sand"
nodes.page: Miles of bare seabed stretch between the old cliffs and the deep water that refuses to return to its accustomed bed, and you keep your head down while your boots move. The march pushes the memory of Orsolya and the Meridian Gear down into the dark. Every gull overhead cries for something lost before the world was mapped. The salt-crust breaks beneath your heels with a sound like dry biscuit-tin lids snapping underfoot, white dust puffing into the still air. Behind you, smoke from Gullmouth's chimneys rises straight and thin into the gray sky. People there still argue over who owns the mud. Your boots keep moving.

exits.label: Step out into the open gray

nodes.title: The Unreturning Tide
nodes.brief: Ending "The Quiet Sand"
nodes.page:
Nothing waits at the end of the dry seabed except more sand and the pale glitter of sun-bleached shells that turn to powder in the wind. You walk until your legs are stiff and your skin is caked in salt-rime. The empty country runs on. No tides have washed these stones for a hundred years. The sun hangs low and red in the west like an unwashed eye behind greasy glass, and long shadows lie across the ribbed dunes. Let the Wreckers keep their silver and let the Brineholders guard their empty pipes; the world has turned another way, and you walk with it.

Boots crunch the crust. Wind works dry across the floor of the lost sea.

nodes.title: The Return
nodes.brief: Ending "Return the Sea Gently"
nodes.page: Cold brine floods the stairs, tasting of old iron and weed-flowers, rising until it laps against your chin and lifts you clear of the stone. Above, the great cog-wheels of the Meridian Gear groan once - a long, rusted sigh like a dying leviathan - before they lock forever in their bronze sockets. The seabed drinks the deluge slowly at first, then all at once as the grey water rushes back into every gutter, cellar, and cove with a clean, shivering roar. Gullmouth wakes to the sound of its own harbour wall taking the blow, boats slamming hard against their mooring ropes, and the smell of wet salt blowing up the cliffs. You drift on the surface of the green surge, staring up through the salt-crusted salt-glass of the skylights as the sun breaks through a low grey cloud. The sea has come home, and the world goes back to waiting for the tide.
